finding.claim: Missing authorization enforcement in update_doc: can_edit() result is discarded, so any user can overwrite any document body. Compare update_title, which correctly calls require_edit().
finding.source: Any authenticated (or any) user sending PUT /doc/<doc_id> with JSON {"body": ...}; doc_id is attacker-chosen
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20 (write to protected document)

trace.note: can_edit(g.user, doc) called but return value ignored; no abort(403)

finding.guards_checked: can_edit returns bool and does not abort (docs.py:7-8); require_edit (docs.py:11-13) would abort but isn't used here. No other auth middleware/before_request in the file; g.user is never set in this file at all, so authentication is also not visible here.

verdict.guard_found: can_edit (docs.py:7-8) returns a bool and is called as a bare statement at docs.py:19, so the result is discarded. require_edit (docs.py:11-13) aborts but is only used in update_title (docs.py:27). No before_request or other auth middleware exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At docs.py:19 the bool from can_edit(g.user, doc) is discarded with no abort(403), so docs.py:20 overwrites doc["body"] for any caller of PUT /doc/<doc_id>. The sibling update_title at docs.py:27 correctly uses require_edit.
